flows.representativeInput: evidence.mjs run (payload CLI) in a temp Git project with .joycraft/local/ ignored and .joycraft/local/evidence-env.json holding a string map
flows.expected: Map names reach the child; CI and JOYCRAFT_EVIDENCE stay 1; result and receipt footer list applied names under env. Fixture {"WORKERS":"3","CI":"0"} prints "3 1" and env ["WORKERS"].

observations.actual: [AC:spec-12-1] passes (2/2 tests, exit 0): the spec fixture prints "3 1"; result.env and footer.env are ["WORKERS"].

Probe via the CLI: spec fixture gives first receipt line "3 1", result env and footer env ["WORKERS"]. A map with JOYCRAFT_EVIDENCE=0 and CI=false gives the child JOYCRAFT_EVIDENCE=1, CI=1, and neither name is listed in env. Values with double spaces, a tab, newlines, quotes, $HOME and backticks reach the child byte-exact (no shell); an empty-string value is applied as empty.

flows.representativeInput: evidence.mjs run with malformed, tracked, staged and absent maps in temp Git projects
flows.expected: Malformed map: exit 2 naming the file. Git-tracked map: exit 2 with "must stay machine-local". No map: runs as before.

observations.actual: [AC:spec-12-2] passes: array, non-string value and invalid JSON each exit 2 with the path in stderr and empty stdout; a committed map exits 2 with "must stay machine-local"; no map exits 0 with no env key and the child sees CI=1.

Probe: array, number value, invalid JSON, null, top-level string, nested object value, null value, boolean value, empty file and a directory at the map path each exit 2, name .joycraft/local/evidence-env.json, and create no receipt (refusal before the child starts). A committed map and an index-only (staged) map exit 2 "must stay machine-local"; tracked-and-malformed exits 2; after git rm --cached the map applies again. No map, and an empty .joycraft/local/ folder, run as before (no env key in result or footer). Installer gitignores .joycraft/local/ (src/install-v1.ts:10).

findings.summary: A map value containing a NUL byte passes validation; spawn then rejects it and the run exits 2 with "Could not start node: ... options.env['A'] must be a string without null bytes", which does not name the map file. Still exit 2 with no receipt.
findings.assumption: JSON strings with \u0000 are rare; the spec decides only non-string values.

findings.summary: Names are not checked: an empty name or a name containing '=' (probe: {"A=B":"c"}) is accepted and listed as applied in env, though the child environment then does not hold that name. Consider refusing names that are not valid variable names.
findings.assumption: The spec says string names; it does not decide name syntax.

findings.summary: CI/JOYCRAFT_EVIDENCE are excluded case-sensitively. On Windows, env names are case-insensitive, so a map key 'ci' or 'Joycraft_Evidence' sits beside CI in the spawn env object and may win; on darwin the probe shows 'ci' stays a separate variable and CI=1. Not checked on Windows.
findings.assumption: POSIX hosts are the main case; the CI matrix runs Windows, so a case-insensitive filter is cheap.

findings.summary: Only a map Git already tracks is refused. A map that is untracked but not ignored (a project whose .gitignore lacks .joycraft/local/) runs, and a later 'git add .' would track it. The installer writes the ignore line, so this needs a hand-edited .gitignore.
findings.assumption: Spec criterion names only a map Git tracks; git check-ignore would close the gap.

limits: Test changes: spec says none; commit 8ec09df adds only the new file tests/runtime-evidence-env.test.ts and changes no existing test file.
The new test file does not cover the JOYCRAFT_EVIDENCE override or values with spaces/newlines; the reviewer probe covers both.
Windows behavior was not run on this machine (darwin).
